subject: SLA duty window proposal & prorata credit outline
messages:
From: Jill Park <procurement@nimbus.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <ops@nimbus.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Clarification: uptime bands / monthly credit proration

Hi Logan,

Thanks for sending the draft SLA earlier. We reviewed the uptime bands and the monthly credit schedule with Finance and a couple of questions came up before we route this to Legal: 

- The template shows a single monthly credit tied to aggregate monthly downtime (example: 98.5% => 5% credit). Can you confirm whether credits are prorated by calendar day or by precise minutes of downtime?
- Our operations team requested a "duty window" carve-out for planned maintenance that impacts scheduled batch inference jobs between 01:00–04:00 PST on Sundays for up to 6 hours. How does Redwood want to classify that (maintenance carveout vs counted downtime)?
- Is there a monthly cap on credits as a % of invoice or a fixed cap? The draft language refers to a "cap" but not how it scales when we run into multiple partial degradations throughout a month.

I'm including a quick spreadsheet (nimbus-sla-questions.xlsx) with scenarios FYI. We need to align on the proration approach and the duty-window mechanics before we progress.

Can we aim to close this this week? We're hoping to finalize the SOW by 11/18.

Best,
Jill Park
Head of Procurement, Nimbus Systems
[Attachment: nimbus-sla-questions.xlsx (XLSX 34KB)]

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Jill Park <procurement@nimbus.com>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <ops@nimbus.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: uptime bands / monthly credit proration

Hi Jill — appreciate the clear scenarios and the spreadsheet. Quick answers up front, and then a proposed compromise: 

- Proration model: Redwood prorates credits strictly by downtime minutes (measured to the second based on incident start/end in our incident system). We calculate the credit as (minutes of unplanned downtime in the month) / (total minutes in month) * invoice amount for the affected service tier, subject to the cap. This avoids rounding mismatch when you see several small degradations.

- Duty window / maintenance: We can include a scheduled-maintenance carveout for customer-approved maintenance slots. For your Sunday 01:00–04:00 PST window, we'll classify events initiated by Nimbus (or pre-approved changes we schedule with you) as maintenance carveouts provided we have a 72-hour notice and the window is registered on the weekly maintenance calendar. Unplanned outages that happen inside that window will still count as downtime unless they are clearly caused by pre-authorized maintenance activities.

- Caps: We propose a dual-cap approach — a per-incident cap equal to 50% of the monthly credit allocation for that service, and a monthly cap at 100% of the monthly invoice for the affected Redwood plan. That keeps exposure bounded for both sides. If you'd prefer a percentage-based cap lower than 100% (e.g., 60%), we can entertain that under a committed-capacity agreement.

Proposed next step: add two sentences to the template to clarify (1) minute-level proration; (2) maintenance registration/notice process and the Sunday duty-window carveout as an example. I've attached a short PDF that shows a worked example for a 30-day month and two partial degradations (proposed-duty-window-model.pdf).

If that looks ok, I'll loop in Legal to issue a redline with the measuring and notice language. If you want to push back on caps, loop me in and I can run numbers with Sales/Finance.

Talk soon,
Logan Wright
Director, Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed-duty-window-model.pdf (PDF 48KB)]

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 13:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Clarification: uptime bands / monthly credit proration

Laura / Ben — forwarding Jill's note and my reply. Summary of the ask: Nimbus wants explicit confirmation that credits are prorated by precise downtime minutes and a maintenance carveout for a recurring 3-hour Sunday window. They also want clarity on the monthly cap behaviour when multiple partial degradations occur.

My proposed posture: commit to minute-level proration (fine), accept a registered duty-window carveout with 72-hour notice (fine), and propose the dual-cap approach (per-incident 50% of monthly credit allocation; monthly cap = 100% of monthly invoice). If they push back on the 100% monthly cap, we can trade to a lower cap in exchange for a 12-month committed volume or an uplift.

Relevant attached files: redlines-nimbus.docx (for Legal redline), proposed-duty-window-model.pdf, nimbus-sla-questions.xlsx.

Can you confirm we should: (A) sign off on minute-level proration language, and (B) keep the monthly cap at 100% unless Sales negotiates committed uplift?

Thanks —
Logan
[Attachment: redlines-nimbus.docx (DOCX 22KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarification: uptime bands / monthly credit proration

Looping in a quick commercial guidance — I agree with minute-level proration; it keeps calculations defensible in audit and reduces disputes. On the cap: 100% monthly invoice cap is industry-standard and protects us; we should hold that as default. If Nimbus pushes to, say, a 60% cap, require either (1) a 12-month committed spend floor at a 10% uplift to list price, or (2) a 6-month trial with a narrow exception for force-majeure only.

On the duty-window carveout: accept registered recurring windows but add a clause that no more than one recurring maintenance window per calendar week is eligible for carveout unless pre-negotiated as part of the SOW. That prevents perverse scheduling across multiple maintenance activities.

If you want, I can draft the exact redline language for Legal to drop into redlines-nimbus.docx. Otherwise go ahead and confirm to Nimbus that we'll have Legal produce the finalized template with the above points.

—Ben
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
